# Theory: The Change is the Object, Not the Branch

Gerrit stores a **change** with a Change-Id, patch sets, and an approval predicate. Branches are an output of submit, not the collaboration primitive.

## Invariants

1. Each push of the same Change-Id is a new patch set (new Git commits).
2. Submit is a server-side integrate (merge/rebase/cherry-pick) after labels.
3. Android/Chromium scale is why this model exists.

```text
refs/for/main  →  change 123 patch set 3
labels  Code-Review+2  Verified+1  →  submit  →  main
```

## What can break

- Treating Gerrit like GitHub PRs (one branch per feature forever).

## How to read this chapter

Model, Change-Ids, CI, ops, practice, lab, when it fits.
